space-001.summary: A star 109 times wider than Earth that shines by its own light and holds the surrounding planets in place with its gravity.
facts: The “il” in the Korean word for Sunday, iryoil, refers to this very star, just as “Sunday” does in English.
Its light takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.

space-002.summary: The smallest planet, racing along the innermost orbit and completing a lap every 88 days.
facts: With almost no atmosphere, it sees temperature swings of more than 600°C between day and night.
In Korean, Wednesday (suyoil) takes its name from this planet, which East Asian tradition calls the “water star.”

space-003.summary: The hottest planet, where heat trapped by a carbon dioxide atmosphere pushes surface temperatures above 460°C.
facts: It takes 243 days to spin once, so its day is longer than its year (225 days).
It is known as the morning star at dawn and the evening star at dusk; in Korean, saetbyeol and gaebapbaragi.

space-004.summary: The only planet known to have liquid water on its surface and to harbor life.
facts: About 70 percent of its surface is ocean.
Its magnetic field and atmosphere shield it from harmful cosmic rays.

space-005.summary: A planet that looks red because of its iron oxide dust, with a day lasting about 24 hours and 40 minutes.
facts: It is home to Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the Solar System.
It has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.

space-006.summary: The largest planet, a gas giant so big that more than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it.
facts: It has the Great Red Spot, a giant storm observed continuously since 1878.
It has 115 known moons, and the four largest were discovered by Galileo Galilei.

space-007.summary: A planet encircled by distinct rings of ice and rock.
facts: Its density is lower than water's, so it is often said that it would float in water.
With 293 known moons, it has more than any other planet.

space-008.summary: A blue-green planet that spins almost on its side, as if rolling along its orbit.
facts: Discovered by William Herschel in 1781, it was the first planet found with a telescope.
Methane in its atmosphere absorbs red light, giving it a blue-green color.

space-009.summary: The planet farthest from the Sun, swept by winds faster than 500 meters per second.
facts: Its existence was worked out by calculation before it was ever spotted through a telescope.
One orbit takes 165 years, so after its discovery in 1846, it did not complete its first full lap until 2011.

space-010.summary: Earth's one and only natural satellite, orbiting 380,000 kilometers away and raising the tides.
facts: In December 2022, South Korea's first space probe, Danuri, entered orbit around it.
In 1969, Apollo 11 landed the first humans on it.

space-011.summary: The moon of Jupiter with the most active volcanoes in the Solar System.
facts: Tidal forces from Jupiter heat its interior, keeping its volcanoes erupting nonstop.
Sulfur colors its surface yellow and red.

space-012.summary: A moon of Jupiter thought to hide an ocean beneath its icy shell.
facts: Its surface is covered in cracked plates of ice.
The Europa Clipper probe, launched in 2024, is set to arrive in 2030.

space-013.summary: Saturn's largest moon, with a thick atmosphere and lakes of methane.
facts: NASA's Dragonfly drone lander is set to launch in 2028 and touch down here in 2034.
In 2005, the Huygens probe landed on its surface.

space-014.summary: A small moon of Saturn that shoots plumes of water into space from its south pole.
facts: The Cassini spacecraft first detected the plumes in 2005.
The particles it sprays out make up part of Saturn's rings.

space-015.summary: An icy world discovered in 1930 that counted as a planet for 76 years before being reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
facts: In 2015, the New Horizons probe made the first close flyby.
Its surface features a heart-shaped plain of ice.

space-016.summary: A dwarf planet discovered in 2005 that was hailed as a possible tenth planet and ended up forcing a new definition of what a planet is.
facts: Its diameter is slightly smaller than Pluto's, but it has more mass.
It is named after the goddess of discord.

space-017.summary: The largest body in the belt between Mars and Jupiter, and the only dwarf planet in the inner Solar System.
facts: The first asteroid ever found, in 1801, it bears the name of the goddess of grain, which shares a root with the word “cereal.”
In 2015, the Dawn spacecraft photographed bright salt deposits inside a crater.

space-018.summary: A band of rocky bodies scattered in orbit between Mars and Jupiter.
facts: All of it combined adds up to only about 3 percent of the Moon's mass.
It is so sparse that spacecraft pass through it safely.

space-019.summary: A doughnut-shaped region of icy bodies spread out beyond Neptune.
facts: Its existence was confirmed in 1992 with the discovery of the first object beyond Pluto.
Short-period comets come from here.

space-020.summary: A very distant home of comets thought to wrap around the Solar System like a sphere.
facts: In 1950, astronomer Jan Oort of the Netherlands proposed its existence.
It remains a hypothetical region that has never been directly observed.

space-021.summary: A moon of Jupiter even larger than Mercury, making it the biggest moon in the Solar System.
facts: It is the only moon known to generate its own magnetic field.
The ocean beneath its ice may hold more water than all the water on Earth's surface combined.

space-022.summary: Jupiter's second-largest moon, with the most densely cratered surface in the Solar System.
facts: Galileo Galilei discovered it in 1610, along with the other three large moons.
The Galileo probe detected signs of a salty ocean beneath its surface.

space-023.summary: Neptune's largest moon, which orbits in the opposite direction to the planet's rotation.
facts: It is thought to be a Kuiper belt object captured by Neptune's gravity.
In 1989, Voyager 2 spotted geysers erupting from its surface.

space-024.summary: Pluto's largest moon, about half as wide as its partner.
facts: It and Pluto always keep the same face toward each other, circling every 6.4 days.
It was discovered in 1978 when a photo of Pluto showed an elongated shape.

space-025.summary: A large moon of Mars that circles the planet three times a day while slowly creeping closer to it.
facts: It drifts 1.8 meters closer every 100 years and could break apart within 50 million years.
Its name is Greek for “fear,” the same root as the word “phobia.”

space-026.summary: The only short-period comet visible to the naked eye, coming back roughly once every 76 years.
facts: It last swung by in 1986 and will return in 2061.
The debris it scatters produces meteor showers in May and October.

space-027.summary: A dwarf planet that spins once every 4 hours, so fast it has been stretched into a rugby-ball shape.
facts: It was the first Kuiper belt object found to have a ring.
It is named after the Hawaiian goddess of fertility.

space-028.summary: A dwarf planet discovered just after Easter 2005, which earned it the nickname “Easterbunny.”
facts: It is about 1,400 kilometers across, roughly three-fifths the size of Pluto.
Its name comes from the god who created humankind in Rapa Nui mythology.

space-029.summary: The second most massive body in the asteroid belt, layered like Earth into crust, mantle and core.
facts: Its south pole holds an impact crater about 500 kilometers wide.
Some of the meteorites that have fallen to Earth broke off from it.
